name: Immad Akhund
profile: Cambridge-educated immigrant founder; Mercury (founded 2017 with Max Tagher and Jason Zhang in San Francisco) is his fourth company and provides banking services to startups and small businesses via partner banks; valued at about $5.2B (May 2026). Previously built and sold Heyzap, a developer tool/ad network for app publishers.
interesting_fact: The Mercury idea came from frustration running Heyzap: 'I'd go to send a wire and it wasn't enabled in my account.' Mercury reportedly gained many customers and deposits after the March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank failure.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting Mercury in 2017 he was a part-time Partner at Y Combinator; meeting Kai Stinchcombe of True Link (debit cards for seniors via a bank partner) at YC's 2013 Demo Day gave him early confidence the bank-partnership model could work.
notes: Very active on X (@immad); also an angel investor (Mercury hosts an investor-database profile for him).

name: Michael Horvath
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Nyfik (software company); co-founder and former CEO of Strava
profile: Harvard economist-turned-founder who co-founded Kana Communications (1996) and then Strava (2009) with Harvard crew teammate Mark Gainey. He was Strava CEO 2009-2013 and again 2019-2023. Since 2024 he runs Nyfik, a small 'stay small but profitable' software company building tools for niche communities.
interesting_fact: Before Strava he was an academic: assistant professor of economics at Stanford (1994-2000) and at Dartmouth's Tuck School (2000-2004), with a PhD from Northwestern; he also captained Harvard's lightweight rowing crew.
deep_cut_fact: His new company's name, Nyfik, is Swedish for 'curious', and its first product is a fog-focused app to help San Francisco locals understand the city's elusive weather.
notes: Industry tag 'Life Sciences' in input is inaccurate; Strava is a fitness/social app. Nyfik's general inbox is the most direct published route.

name: Tom Leathes
profile: British serial entrepreneur who co-founded Motorway with long-time partners Harry Jones and Alex Buttle; Motorway lets consumers sell cars to a network of dealers and reached a ~$1B valuation. Motorway is the trio's fifth startup after Acre (recruitment), LoanCube, Official Space and Top10 (a hotel recommendation app closed in 2015).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders have worked together for about 20 years; three of their earlier startups had 'moderately successful' exits, and he calls Motorway's success the product of '20 years of building start-ups, making mistakes and learning from them.'
deep_cut_fact: Motorway began after the founders spent about six months in an office deciding what to build; they launched an instant car-valuation website, then phoned sellers and cold-called dealers themselves to place cars. Leathes joked he's 'glad they're not recorded.'
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Secret Leaders, Riding Unicorns); Motorway press office is the published route.

name: Kazuhide Sekiyama
current_role: Co-founder & Representative Executive Officer, Spiber Inc. (Tsuruoka, Yamagata, Japan)
profile: Japanese biotech entrepreneur who began researching artificial spider silk as a Keio University biotechnology student and founded Spiber (spider + fiber) during his doctoral studies. Spiber engineers microbes to ferment protein materials; it has shifted from replicating spider silk ('Qmonos') to Brewed Protein fibers for apparel, sold to fashion partners.
interesting_fact: Sekiyama and co-founder Junichi Sugahara were named to the Vogue Business 2025 100 Innovators list (Entrepreneurs and Founders category).
deep_cut_fact: Spiber grew out of a seminar at Keio's Institute for Advanced Biosciences in Tsuruoka under Prof. Masaru Tomita; in 2007 Sekiyama (then a 4th-year student) and Sugahara, joined by his high-school classmate and CPA Hideya Mizutani, made their first batch of synthetic protein fiber before incorporating.
notes: Japanese name 関山和秀. Company is based in rural Tsuruoka rather than Tokyo; contact form is the published route (no press email found).

name: Jaswinder Chadha
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Axtria Inc. (life-sciences data/analytics software, New Jersey)
profile: Jaswinder 'Jassi' Chadha co-founded Axtria in 2010, building it into a cloud software and analytics provider for pharma commercial operations (sales, marketing, data management) valued around $1B. An IIT Delhi mechanical engineer with operations-research graduate training (UTEP, Texas A&M), he has worked with 100+ global companies.
interesting_fact: Twice named E&Y Entrepreneur of the Year; also received the Pharmaceutical Management Science Association Lifetime Achievement Award and IIT Delhi's Distinguished Alumni Award (2022).
deep_cut_fact: He endowed a Chair in Operations Research at IIT Delhi (2008) and a Chair in Data Analytics (2021) named after himself and his mother, who in 1968 became the first woman to earn a maths PhD from IIT Delhi - making them IIT Delhi's first parent-child graduates.
notes: Goes by 'Jassi'. Co-founder Navdeep Chadha is CTO. A 2022 press release listed an individual Axtria media contact; the general connect@ inbox is the stable published route.

name: Dror Shimoni
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, HoneyBook (runs its Israel R&D center) - per Calcalist profile; current title not re-confirmed on HoneyBook's site
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Oz and Naama Alon. HoneyBook is a San Francisco-based clientflow/business-management platform (CRM, contracts, invoicing, payments) for freelancers and small service businesses, valued at $2.2B in 2021. Shimoni leads engineering from the Tel Aviv R&D office.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook's concept came from Naama Alon planning her wedding in Tel Aviv and finding no tools to organize event vendors; the platform has since processed over $13B in transactions for small businesses.
deep_cut_fact: He was a programmer at SAP Software Solutions; when Naama Alon proposed the three founders quit their day jobs, he handed in his resignation the next day. When the others moved to the US for a Palo Alto accelerator, he stayed in Israel and built the R&D center.
notes: Low public profile; the Alons are HoneyBook's public faces. Best route is the HoneyBook press team.

name: Meng Jiange
current_role: Executive Director & Chairman, GenScript Biotech Corp. (HKEX: 1548), parent of Probio; also a director of Legend Biotech
profile: Most likely Robin (Jiange) Meng, chairman of GenScript, whose CDMO subsidiary Probio provides biologics and cell/gene-therapy manufacturing services; GenScript announced plans in Sept 2026 to spin off Probio on the HKEX. A finance executive with 30+ years' experience, he joined GenScript as CFO (c. 2010-2017) and became chairman around 2020.
interesting_fact: Before GenScript he was CFO of Quay Magnesium (2008-2010), Asia finance controller at Saint-Gobain's Grains and Powder division, and held finance roles at Schering-Plough China and Guangdong Whirlpool.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer - a Bachelor of Engineering from Changsha Communications Institute (now Changsha University of Science & Technology) - before earning a Master's in finance from Queen's University at Kingston, Canada.
notes: Identity match is probable but not confirmed: Hurun lists him as a Probio 'founder', while GenScript names Frank Zhang, Sally Wang and Larry Wang as co-founders and Meng as chairman. Also known as Robin Meng / Jian Ge Meng.

name: Alexis Angot
current_role: Co-founder and former CFO of Ÿnsect; current role not found in public sources
profile: French finance executive (ESSEC) who co-founded Ÿnsect in Paris in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Jean-Gabriel Levon and Fabrice Berro. Ÿnsect farmed mealworms for animal-feed protein and fertilizer, raised about €600M and reached unicorn status; Angot served as CFO before stepping down. The company was placed in judicial liquidation in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Ÿnsect was founded by four scientists and environmental activists, became the second company in the world authorised (by ANSES, 2020) to market a natural insect-based fertilizer, and earned B Corp certification in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In episode #8 of the 'Tomorrow Now' podcast (Oct 2023), billed as 'when the financier becomes an industry builder', he discussed taking Ÿnsect from idea to industrial company, why he chose to leave the CFO role, and how a board should work best.
notes: Sensitive: Ÿnsect went into safeguard (2024) and liquidation (Dec 2025) amid political criticism of public funding - avoid in outreach. No published contact found; LinkedIn would be the likely route but was not verified.

name: Gaston Taratuta
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aleph Group (formerly Aleph Holding), Miami
profile: Argentine entrepreneur (b. 1972) whose Aleph Group acts as commercial/advertising partner for platforms such as X, TikTok and Spotify in markets where they don't operate directly. It grew from IMS Internet Media Services (2005); CVC's 2021 minority investment valued Aleph at about $2B. Aleph has since expanded into payments (Aleph Payments, Localpayment).
interesting_fact: He was named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 - the first Argentine to win the global award.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding IMS he spent six years at Brazilian internet company UOL's Miami office, leaving in 2004 as head of international operations; by his own account he started IMS in 2005 with about US$5,000, and from 2011 it represented Twitter commercially abroad.
notes: Full name Christian Gastón Taratuta. No press email published on the company site; the company X account is @itsalephdigital.

name: Marcelo Jacques
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Dock (Brazilian payments & banking-as-a-service platform, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2020-2021; not re-confirmed for 2026
profile: Brazilian fintech executive and former investment banker (TMT coverage) who serves as Chief Strategy Officer of Dock, the São Paulo paytech formed when Conductor unified Conductor, Dock and Muxi under one brand in 2021. Dock provides card processing, digital accounts and BaaS infrastructure to 200+ companies across Latin America.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Conductor said it processed more than R$10B in monthly transactions across 100M customer accounts while staying profitable; Jacques: 'we always look for the correct balance between growth and profitability.'
notes: Low public profile; CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's main public face. Press room lists both an in-house inbox and an agency inbox.
